Do the following using the steps provided in their respective sections.
        Steps:
        1. clone the repo git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
        2. analyse the contents of the repo and create following.
            2.1 create/update dockerfile based on the analysis.

            2.3 github actions file to build application on pushing to main branch.
        3. add all changed file to git changes

function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** that you can copy‑paste into your terminal (or run in a script).  
It covers everything you asked for:

1. **Clone the repo**  
2. **Analyse** the repo (I’ve made a few assumptions – see the “Assumptions” section)  
3. **Create** the Dockerfile, Kubernetes YAMLs and GitHub Actions workflow  
4. **Add / Commit / Push** the changes

> ⚠️ **NOTE** – I can’t actually run `git clone` or `git push` from here, but the commands below will do it for you on your machine.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the repository

```bash
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse the repo & create the artefacts

### 2.1 Assumptions about the repo

| File | What I saw / assumed |
|------|----------------------|
| `package.json` | Contains a `start` script that runs `node app.js` |
| `app.js` | Listens on `process.env.PORT || 3000` |
| `README.md` | Basic description |
| No existing Dockerfile, Kubernetes or GitHub Actions files |

> If any of these assumptions are wrong, feel free to tweak the generated files accordingly.

### 2.2 Dockerfile

Create a file named `Dockerfile` in the repo root:

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
# ------------------------------------
# Base image – lightweight Node runtime
FROM node:18-alpine

# Working directory inside the container
WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files first to leverage Docker cache
COPY package*.json ./

# Install production dependencies only
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the application
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Default command
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> **Why `node:18-alpine`?**  
> Alpine is small, fast, and the latest LTS (18.x) is stable for most Node apps.

### 2.3 Kubernetes YAMLs

Create a file named `k8s/nodejs-welcome.yaml` (you can keep it in a `k8s/` folder or at the repo root):

```yaml
# k8s/nodejs-welcome.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
        env:
        - name: NODE_ENV
          value: production
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

> **What this does**  
> * Deployment: 2 replicas, pulls image from GitHub Container Registry (`ghcr.io`).  
> * Service: Exposes the pods on port 80 inside the cluster (ClusterIP).

### 2.4 GitHub Actions workflow

Create a file at `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
name: CI / Build & Push

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # Checkout the repo
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Set up Docker Buildx (needed for multi‑arch builds)
      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      # Log in to GitHub Container Registry
      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Build and push the Docker image
      - name: Build & push Docker image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:latest

      # Optional: Run tests (if you have a test script)
      # - name: Run tests
      #   run: npm test
```

> **What it does**  
> * Triggers on pushes to `main`.  
> * Builds the Docker image and pushes it to `ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest`.  
> * Uses the built‑in `GITHUB_TOKEN` for authentication – no extra secrets needed.

---

## 3️⃣ Add the new files to Git

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s/nodejs-welcome.yaml .github/workflows/ci.yml
```

If you want to keep the `k8s/` folder, make sure it exists:

```bash
mkdir -p k8s
```

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & Push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

> After pushing, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically run and push the Docker image to GHCR.

---

## 🎉 Done!

You now have:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Builds a lightweight Node image |
| `k8s/nodejs-welcome.yaml` | Deployment + Service for Kubernetes |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | CI pipeline that builds & pushes the image |

Feel free to tweak the image tag, number of replicas, or any environment variables to match your production needs. Happy coding!
